Before the light, the meadow is a sea without a shore.
Every blade holds a little of the night.
Then warmth begins to move across the field.
The grass answers, one stem at a time.
A whole sky rests inside a drop of dew.
Above the green, the seed heads open to the air.
By noon, the wind has found its way through everything.
Wave follows wave. There is no hurry here.
A passing shower darkens the earth beneath them.
And when the clouds move on, each slender stem is gold.
The day lets go slowly, leaving its warmth among the seeds.
Small lights rise where the shadows gather.
The field grows quiet. The growing does not stop.
